newsitem.title: USA: U.S. congressional study sees economic expansion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. congressional study sees economic expansion.

text.p: The U.S. economic expansion has been sustained partly due to the Federal Reserve's "credible" anti-inflationary monetary policy, and is expected to continue, a Joint Economic Committee study said Wednesday.
"The reason for this expected continued expansion is that no important imbalances have emerged that typically have derailed expansions in the past," the report said.
"In particular, inflation appears to be in check with little evidence of an imminent resurgence," the report by the committee's chief macroeconomist Robert Keleher said.
Export growth due to lower trade barriers has helped sustain the expansion, the report said. A relatively stable U.S. dollar has also helped foster export growth, the study said.
"Inflation should remain well contained with the Fed's likely continued commitment to price stability," the report said. It was written before the Fed raised interest rates last week.
